full_judgment:
Mr. Gour Gopal Saha, J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 31.10.2000 passed by the Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Additional Court No. 2, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 56 of 1998 decreeing the suit on contest for an amount of Tk. 15,63,395.50. 

 2. It appears that the appellants have tiled the present appeal without depositing 50% of the decretal amount in the trial Court before preferring the appeal before this court as enjoined by Section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990, which specifically provides that any person aggrieved by a decree passed by an Artha Rin Adalat must deposit at least 50% of the decretal money in the trial Court before preferring an appeal before the High Court Division. 

 3. This special provision in a special law has been enacted with the specific purpose of prompt realization of at least half of the decretal dues from the .judgment debtors following the decree passed by an Artha Rin Adalat so that a financial institution is not required to wait for an unlimited period for realization of a substantial portion of the decretal dues pending disposal of the appeal preferred by the judgment-debtors. 

 4. Law clearly provides for deposit of at least 50% of the decretal amount in cash in the trial court within 30 days of the decree as a condition precedent for preferring an appeal before the High Court Division. The provision for deposit of at least 50% of the decretal money in the trial Court has obviously a definite implication. A bank guarantee, which is merely a promise to pay in the future on the happening of certain things is certainly not a substitute for the statutory requirement of payment in cash of at least half of the decretal dues as a condition precedent for preferring an appeal before the High Court Division.
